entries.title: Samhain
entries.text: 1 November is the old Irish quarter day that opens the winter half of the year. In the old reckoning the year began here, with the darkest months to follow.
entries.someplacessay: Some older accounts keep the festival on the evening of 31 October, since the old day was counted from nightfall.
sources: Quarter-day dates in standard Irish calendar references (to be cited properly)

entries.title: Lá na Marbh, All Souls' Day
entries.text: Traditionally this is the day for remembering the dead. Families said prayers and many parishes read out the names of the departed.
entries.someplacessay: Customs differ by parish. In some places the dead were also remembered on the night before.
sources: Folklore overviews of Irish November customs (to be cited properly)

entries.title: An Geimhreadh, winter
entries.text: Irish gives the four seasons their own names, and the old year counts winter from Samhain: Geimhreadh, then Earrach, Samhradh and Fómhar.
entries.someplacessay: Weather forecasters count winter from 1 December instead. Both are in use.
sources: Irish dictionary entries for the season names (to be cited properly)
